evidence: Table 2-2 row: "Decode: bandwidth verdict, hypothetical single-device aggregate ... bandwidth-bound ... This row compares aggregate bytes against a single device’s bandwidth, and a 140-GB FP16 model does not fit on one 80-GB H100: the row illustrates the roofline point, not a deployable layout"
issue: The table row is labeled "bandwidth-bound" and uses a hypothetical single-device aggregate, but the same table later says weight-read bandwidth is not binding on the canonical 8×H100 host (700 GB/s < 3.35 TB/s). The row is correct as scoped, but its placement and label invite readers to treat a non-deployable single-device comparison as a system verdict.
fix_instruction: Move the hypothetical single-device row to a clearly marked sidebar or add a row-level label such as "illustrative single-device only; not the host verdict" so the deployable host conclusion is not visually conflated with the aggregate comparison.

evidence: "The minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline is four, not eight ... ⌈1.19 PFLOPS ÷ (0.989 × 0.35)⌉ ≈ 4 GPUs meet it"
issue: The phrase "minimum GPU count" is locally scoped as a per-request prefill-feasibility count, but it reads as a deployable GPU-count recommendation. The same paragraph later says the canonical 8-GPU choice is driven by concurrency, KV capacity and headroom, so the two numbers are not alternatives.
fix_instruction: Rename the phrase to "minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline under the stated MFU assumption" and repeat the non-deployability caveat immediately after the arithmetic.

evidence: "Compute the cost on the fleet $/hr ÷ fleet rps basis (5 × $20/hr ÷ 40 rps ≈ ~$0.0007 per request at peak, against 21 × $20/hr ÷ 40 rps ≈ ~$0.0029 at 9.2K input)"
issue: The displayed expression omits the 3,600 s/hr conversion; as written, dividing dollars per hour by requests per second does not yield dollars per request. The intended value is correct only when the hour-to-second conversion is applied.

evidence: "The ~436 GB KV budget (640 − 140 − 64, §5.3(b)) supports ~436/24.9 ≈ 17.5, i.e. 17 whole-slot concurrent 9,500-token requests per host ... against the initial 9.2K KV alone the quotient is ≈18 (436 ÷ 24.1), matching Ch 4 §4.6."
issue: The text says "supports ~436/24.9 ≈ 17.5, i.e. 17 whole-slot" but does not explicitly state that the 17 is a floor and that the input-only 18 is not used for fleet sizing. The distinction is stated elsewhere, but this occurrence can be read as two competing concurrency ceilings.
fix_instruction: Add "floored to 17; the input-only quotient of 18 is shown only for reconciliation and is not the slot-counting basis" after the first quotient.

evidence: PDF p.90, Canonical Workload box: "TTFT SLO: 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); p95 ≤ 2 s" and "TPOT SLO: 25 ms/token; p95 ≤ 35 ms". The Preface (PDF p.22) explicitly states: "TTFTmodelled = retrieval + prefill = 1.2 s — a two-term modelled budget, never the TTFT SLO and never TTFTe2e." Table 4-1 on PDF p.84 correctly labels the same values "TTFT budget 1.2 s" and "TPOT budget ~25 ms/token". Section 4.3 on PDF p.102 confirms: "1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
issue: The Canonical Workload box field labels 1.2 s as "TTFT SLO" and 25 ms as "TPOT SLO", directly contradicting the Preface's explicit naming instruction ("never the TTFT SLO"), Table 4-1's correct "TTFT budget" / "TPOT budget" labels (same chapter, same section), and §4.3's statement that pass/fail is judged against the 2 s p95 ceiling, not the 1.2 s budget. A reader consulting only the Canonical Workload box would conclude 1.2 s is the pass/fail SLO threshold, which the book elsewhere says it is not.
fix_instruction: Rename both fields in the Canonical Workload box from "TTFT SLO" to "TTFT budget" and from "TPOT SLO" to "TPOT budget", matching Table 4-1 and §4.3. Alternatively, add a parenthetical like "(design budget; SLO ceiling: p95 ≤ 2 s)" to make the distinction explicit. Scan for other occurrences of "SLO" paired with the 1.2 s / 25 ms budget values rather than the 2 s / 35 ms ceiling values.

page: PDF p.39 (printed p.15); also PDF p.45 (printed p.21) and PDF p.49 (printed p.24)
evidence: Chapter opening claim (PDF p.39): "why, at the canonical low-batch operating point, decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound while prefill is compute-bound". §2.2 (PDF p.45): "In the canonical operating point — low batch — decode is bandwidth-bound. It is like pushing the water of that same 140 GB reservoir through a standard garden hose. On a single device, the full 140 GB must stream within each 25 ms step to produce one token" ... followed by "(The 140 GB hose is the single-device illustration. On the canonical 8×H100 host, each GPU streams only its 17.5 GB shard per step, which takes ~5.2 ms at peak — 21% of the 25 ms step.)" But Table 2-2 (PDF p.49) concludes for the same host: "Decode: bandwidth verdict, canonical 8×H100 host (TP = 8) | bandwidth not binding at this point (weight-read only) | 700 GB/s < 3.35 TB/s → ... 21% of the 25 ms TPOT step, so weight-read bandwidth is not the binding constraint at this operating point", and Ch 6 Table 6-1 (PDF p.145) repeats: "weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% achieved HBM util".
issue: The headline verdict of the chapter ("at the canonical low-batch operating point, decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound") is asserted for the canonical operating point, but the chapter's own arithmetic shows that on the canonical 8×H100 host the decode weight-read consumes only ~21% of peak HBM bandwidth and is therefore NOT the binding resource; the 5.6 TB/s figure that produces the "bandwidth-bound" verdict comes from a hypothetical single-device layout the book itself says is not deployable (140 GB FP16 does not fit in one 80 GB H100). The book elsewhere separates "regime classification by arithmetic intensity" (~1 FLOP/byte) from "the binding constraint" (which has headroom), but the chapter's framing sentence and §2.2's water analogy state the bandwidth-bound verdict as a property of "the canonical operating point". A reader who takes the chapter framing as the canonical verdict would mis-diagnose the canonical decode path (the actual binding terms there are the TP collectives, kernel efficiency, sampling and scheduling, plus the 9.2K KV attention read).
fix_instruction: In the chapter opening and §2.2, restate the decode verdict as a regime/classification statement (arithmetic intensity ~1 FLOP/byte at low batch) and explicitly state that on the canonical 8×H100 host the weight-read is NOT bandwidth-saturated (~21% of peak), so the binding terms at that operating point are TP collectives, kernel efficiency, sampling/scheduling and the KV attention read. Reserve "bandwidth-bound" for the hypothetical single-device case and label it as such wherever it appears in the chapter.

page: PDF p.123 (printed p.99); supporting text PDF p.121 (printed p.97) and PDF p.124 (printed p.100)
evidence: Table 5-2 rows (PDF p.123): "Selection status | recommended, pending target-corpus validation | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]" and "Verdict | Embedding: all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim); Generation: 70B FP16 on 8×H100 | Selection surfaces (§5.1) [canonical scenario][DERIVED]". But §5.3(a) (PDF p.121) states the quality basis of that verdict: "Assume, as a scenario input rather than a measured result, a quality-vs-dimension uplift of up to ~15% MAP [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] (a chosen input, not a cited finding — no study is invoked here)", and the same section hedges the recommendation ("the quality claim itself is the §5.3(a)/§5.7 item still to validate on the target corpus"). The chapter's own rule (PDF p.124, Table 5-2 note): "The mixed-input convention therefore governs: the non-canonical input wins, and the rows carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] rather than [canonical scenario][DERIVED]".
issue: Provenance/label mismatch: the Table 5-2 verdict and selection-status rows carry [canonical scenario] provenance even though the embedding-model recommendation's decisive input is explicitly an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] (~15% MAP uplift) whose transfer to the target corpus is an open [HYPOTHESIS]. Under the chapter's own stated mixed-input convention (non-canonical input wins → [ILLUSTRATIVE]), these two rows are mislabeled. The error matters because the two provenance tags are the book's mechanism for telling a reader which numbers survive re-derivation against a real corpus and a procured quote.
fix_instruction: Relabel the Table 5-2 "Selection status" and "Verdict" rows to [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] / [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] respectively (or split the row so the generation-model verdict keeps [canonical scenario][DERIVED] while the embedding-model verdict carries [ILLUSTRATIVE]), and add the same mixed-input note that the per-dollar rows already carry.

evidence: Table 6-1, Decode row, "Resource tell" cell: "batch-1 single-device illustration only: high HBM util, low FLOP util (at the canonical point HBM util is ~21%, not saturated)". The same row's Verdict cell: "memory-bound by intensity (~1.0 FLOP/byte ≪ ridge ~295); weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% achieved HBM util".
issue: The diagnostic cell contradicts itself inside one cell: it names "high HBM util" as the telemetry tell for a bandwidth-bound decode, and then states that at the canonical operating point HBM utilization is ~21%, i.e. not high and not saturated. Ch 6's stated purpose is to let a reader "tell bandwidth-bound from compute-bound purely from the counters", so a tell that does not hold at the book's own canonical operating point is a defect in the diagnostic instruction, not just awkward phrasing.
fix_instruction: Split the cell into two explicit cases: the single-device batch-1 illustration (tell: high HBM util, low FLOP util) and the canonical 8×H100 TP=8 operating point (tell: low-to-moderate HBM util (~21%), and the binding evidence is TP-collective/kernel/scheduling overhead plus KV-attention traffic, with MFU/queue-depth as the observable).

page: PDF p.52 (printed p.28) vs PDF p.76 (printed p.52) and PDF p.88 (printed p.64)
evidence: Ch 2 §2.3 (PDF p.52): "At FP16 (2 bytes per parameter), the weight footprint is W = N ×2 = 140 GB" — here W denotes the weight footprint in bytes. Ch 4 (PDF p.76): "Little's Law, L = λW, relates the average number of requests in the defined system L, the arrival rate λ, and the mean time in system W" — here W denotes mean service time. Ch 4 Canonical Workload box (PDF p.88): "the occupancy service time is Wexec ≈ 8.6 s" and separately "Mean request service time (planning headline — not used for occupancy) ~10 s".
issue: Symbol collision across chapters: W is used for two unrelated quantities (weight bytes in Ch 2; mean time in system in Ch 4, where it is also the multiplier in the book's most-used formula L = λW). The book goes out of its way to reserve other symbols explicitly ("the active-user population is written U; C is reserved throughout the book for a host's KV slot capacity"), so this is an inconsistency with the book's own notation discipline; a reader crossing from Ch 2's "W = 140 GB" into Ch 4's "λW" can misread one as the other.
fix_instruction: Rename the Ch 2 weight-footprint symbol (e.g. W_bytes or M_weights) and keep W reserved for mean time in system throughout, adding the reservation to the Preface's reading-conventions list alongside U and C.

evidence: Table 7-1, row "3×H100 total VRAM", derivation cell reads in full: "3× the vendor's 80 GB per-part constant [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); tagged as the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2 are" — the sentence ends on the word "are" with no predicate, and the same table's "2×H100 total VRAM" and "8×H100 total VRAM" rows carry complete derivations ("2 ×80 GB = 160 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)", "8 ×80 GB = 640 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)").
issue: Truncated/incomplete derivation cell: the 3×H100 row's label text is missing its ending clause (apparently a note such as "…are tagged [1P][FACT] as well"), leaving a dangling predicate. Because this table is the book's anchor memory ledger, a half-finished label under a numeric row that feeds the "≥3×H100" conclusion is a visible production defect.
fix_instruction: Complete the 3×H100 derivation cell (e.g. "3 × 80 GB = 240 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); like the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2, the capacity is a [1P][FACT] vendor constant") and proof the table for other truncated cells.

evidence: In-figure label in Fig 6.2 reads "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" and "SLO-violating region (> 2 s)". The figure caption states the opposite convention: "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget — a superset of TTFT violations". Ch 4 §4.3 makes the distinction explicit: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
issue: Figure-vs-caption/labelling mismatch: the in-figure legend calls the 2 s line the "TTFT budget", which is the book's term for the 1.2 s design budget (TTFT budget 1.2 s, retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s). The caption itself flags the correct reading (p95 ceiling). A reader reading only the graphic will apply the wrong threshold name to the wrong line, and the same line is used in Ch 6's text as "the 2 s SLO" / "the p95 TTFT-ceiling line".
fix_instruction: Change the in-figure label from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s (SLO)" (and, if both lines are wanted, add the 1.2 s design-budget line separately), matching the caption's terminology and Table 4-2's naming.

chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload (§4.6, Memory planning)
evidence: "That 17-slot ceiling is a per-host figure, and its binding limit is per-rank: an 80 GB rank runs 99.97% full at 17.5 slots (Ch 7 §7.3 technical note), so the per-rank test — not this pool-level arithmetic — decides residency." (PDF p. 112, book p. 88)
issue: Dangling cross-reference. Ch 7 §7.3 (PDF pp. 155–171) contains no section or box called a "technical note" and never states the 99.97% figure; its only named notes are "Note on 'does it fit?'" and "Attention-family sensitivity note". A reader who follows the citation to verify the per-rank residency claim (which §4.6 explicitly says "decides residency") finds nothing. The underlying arithmetic is correct (17.5 slots × 3.11296 GB/rank-slot + 17.5 GB weights + 8 GB reserve = 79.98 GB of 80 GB ≈ 99.97%) but the derivation is cited to a target that does not visibly exist.
fix_instruction: Add the per-rank fill computation as an explicitly named "technical note" in Ch 7 §7.3, or repoint the citation to wherever the per-rank 99.97% figure is actually derived.

chapter: Ch. 3 — Understanding the Model (§3.6.2); recurrence in Ch. 5 fn. 3–4, Ch. 7 §7.3.2, §7.3.3
evidence: "at about 27B total and about 14B active parameters as published (Wan2.2 source, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28)" (PDF p. 72). Contrast Ch 2 §2.1.2 (PDF p. 44), same source: "pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028". Preface policy (PDF p. 21): "a separately dated 2026-10-28 technology notes in the body and Appendix A carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028".
issue: Inconsistent application of the book's own post-cutoff labeling rule. The Preface states that dated 2026-10-28 notes carry the revision identifier v20260913+addendum-20261028, and Ch 2 §2.1.2 and Ch 7 §7.3.1 do carry it. But other 2026-10-28 citations omit the identifier: Ch 3 §3.6.2 (Wan2.2, PDF p. 72), Ch 5 footnote 3 (PDF pp. 119–120) and footnote 4 (PDF p. 130) — these say "post-cutoff addendum" but no revision ID — Ch 7 §7.3.2 ("released configuration, retrieved 2026-10-28", PDF p. 162), and Ch 7 §7.3.3 ("GGUF specification, pinned revision, retrieved 2026-10-28", PDF p. 166). The addendum revision identifier is the reader's only anchor into the Edition-history addendum log, so the omission breaks the traceability the policy promises — notably for the identical Wan2.2 source that Ch 2 tags and Ch 3 does not.
fix_instruction: Add "v20260913+addendum-20261028" to every dated 2026-10-28 citation (Ch 3 §3.6.2; Ch 5 fn. 3–4; Ch 7 §7.3.2; Ch 7 §7.3.3), or narrow the Preface rule to name exactly which notes carry the identifier.

chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference (§2.3, Canonical host verdict)
evidence: "1.29 PFLOP / (8 × 0.989 PFLOPS) = 0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU [2°: industry benchmarks][ASSUMPTION — the book's planning MFU, with 25/35/45% sensitivity in Ch 8, Table 8-1]" (PDF p. 54, book p. 30)
issue: Evidence-label pairing violates the book's own definition. The Preface evidence panel and Table 4-2 Note 1 define ASSUMPTION as "a deliberately chosen scenario input, paired with a scenario provenance ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE])". Here ASSUMPTION is paired with [2°], while the parenthetical itself identifies the value as a book-chosen planning constant ("the book's planning MFU"). By the book's taxonomy an externally benchmarked norm used to set a target takes [2°] provenance (Table 4-1 table-level note), but the epistemic partner for an author-chosen planning value should be a scenario provenance.
fix_instruction: Relabel as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (keeping the 25/35/45% sensitivity pointer to Ch 8 Table 8-1), or amend the ASSUMPTION definition to permit benchmark-informed planning constants.

chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token (§1.1.2); recurrence in Ch. 7 §7.1.1 and §7.2.1
evidence: "the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model [HYPOTHESIS]" (PDF p. 27, book p. 3). Also Ch 7 §7.1.1 caveat box ending "...before that budget's arithmetic is reused for a different generation mechanism. [DERIVED]" and Ch 7 §7.2.1 ending "...so video keys and values cannot simply be retained as immutable prefix entries for every later step. [DERIVED]" (both PDF p. 154)
issue: Bare Axis-2 evidence tags with no Axis-1 provenance partner. The Preface states: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes" and "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair". The tagged [HYPOTHESIS] in Ch 1 and the boxed [DERIVED] caveats in Ch 7 carry only the epistemic tag, so the provenance axis is missing exactly where the book's discipline says it must be present.
fix_instruction: Add provenance partners (e.g. [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] for the context-window range claim; [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for the two Ch 7 caveat boxes), or add a stated exception for caveat-box tags in the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter.

chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload (§4.8 mini-case, Label note)
evidence: "This 5,000-employee growth variant is non-canonical, so its inputs (5,000 employees, 10% peak activity, 50 rps, and the ~8.6 s engine response duration) carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" (PDF p. 115, book p. 91)
issue: Provenance misattribution of an inherited canonical value. The ~8.6 s engine response duration is not an input of the growth variant — it is the canonical W_exec ≈ 8.58 s, derived in Table 4-2 as [canonical scenario][DERIVED] ("Wexec = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode = 8.58 s, shown as 8.6 s") and reused unchanged in this same mini-case's arithmetic ("50 × 8.6 ≈ 430") and in Ch 6 §6.8. Listing it as an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] input gives the same quantity two conflicting labels across chapters and leaves ambiguous whether the variant assumes an independent service time.
fix_instruction: State that the variant inherits W_exec ≈ 8.6 s from the canonical scenario (Table 4-2), and restrict the [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] list to the genuinely new inputs (5,000 employees, 10% peak activity, 50 rps).

issue: The text contains a formatting error in Section 7.7. There is a bullet point character '•' followed by an empty line or space, and then the next item '(a) decode-time...' is formatted as a separate line rather than a second bullet item, or the first bullet was left incomplete.

chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
evidence: PDF p.161 says: “The 24 GB device is an illustrative placeholder with no vendor model named, and no number from this subsection is used anywhere else in the book — it is a geometry example, not a hardware recommendation.” The same subsection later says: “Device capacities are first-party specifications (Intel Arc Pro B70 datasheet, B65 datasheet, Arc Pro B60 datasheet), retrieved 2026-10-28.”
issue: The subsection first says no vendor model is named, then names vendor device datasheets in support of the same capacity discussion. This is a local provenance/clarity contradiction about whether the 24 GB device example is vendor-neutral or vendor-backed.
